payment.actual_conclusion: For every real tau, the universal implication tau*u_A >= C_old => P+Delta >= freshOPT_2 holds exactly for tau<=1. For every tau>1 the same six-label four-player policy with integer customer vector w0+k*e supplies a complete SPE and deficit -1.
payment.derivation: At tau<=1, u_A>=0 makes the premise imply u_A>=C_old; the four nonnegative multipliers yield the conclusion for any legal two-player residual background. At tau>1, both w0 and e satisfy every ordered-history incentive row of the same policy. Homogeneity preserves w0+k e. Along actual AB, u_A=8+k, C_old=34/3+k, P=17+2k, Delta=0 and freshOPT_2=18+2k. Choose integer k>=max(0,ceil(10/(3(tau-1))-8)). All original nodes, labels and off-path weak ties remain.
payment.boundary: This is a threshold for an additional old-cover payment assumption. Root 2W-OPT4=16+2k remains positive. It does not solve the universal root half conjecture.

adjacent.actual_conclusion: An adjacent unit-load pair Q=P+a, a in {0,1}, has exactly one nonnegative integer joint count table iff F_L(c-1)<=F_M(c)<=F_L(c).
adjacent.proof: X_c=F_L(c)-F_M(c), Y_c=F_M(c)-F_L(c-1); these are necessary by L_c=X_c+Y_c and M_c=Y_c+X_(c-1). The interlacing inequalities give nonnegative integers; equal finite totals force X at the tail to zero, recovering both marginal arrays.
adjacent.boundary: Unique joint counts do not identify indexed history pairing, actual own/H source shares, the complete SPE or a root payment. A terminal/pair transport application must retain the same target tuple, all source A/H data and the declared product-fibre domain.
